t: By one account a proto-Khoe people emerged between 400 BCE and 100 CE in southern Zimbabwe, as San peoples met herding communities drifting south from East Africa; with their sheep and later cattle, Khoekhoe herders spread south to the Cape.
In 1510 ox-mounted ǃUriǁ’aekua defeated the party of Francisco de Almeida at the Battle of Salt River, killing him and fifty of his men.
Smallpox, land seizure and war under Dutch rule broke up Khoekhoe society, and in German South-West Africa from 1904 to 1907 over 10,000 Nama, more than half the people, may have died.
dyk: The International Astronomical Union has named the star Mu¹ Scorpii Xami di mûra, “eyes of the lion”, after its traditional name in the Khoekhoe language.
ev: By Mellet’s account a proto-Khoe people emerges in southern Zimbabwe as San peoples meet herders from East Africa
Widespread Khoekhoe settlements and large herds appear south of the Orange River
Ox-mounted ǃUriǁ’aekua defeat and kill Francisco de Almeida at the Battle of Salt River
Georg Schmidt founds Genadendal among the Khoe-speaking peoples, the first mission station in southern Africa
The Kat River Settlement gives Khoekhoe land of their own near the eastern frontier of the Cape Colony
The Cape franchise gives the vote to men meeting a low property test, regardless of colour
In the war with German forces in German South-West Africa more than half of the Nama may die
Apartheid ends, and with it the racial designation “Coloured” imposed on some Khoekhoe

f.homeland: Southern Africa, from southern Zimbabwe, northern Botswana and the Limpopo south to the Cape; today the Nama of Namibia, Botswana and South Africa (Great and Little Namaqualand), the Damara of Namibia, the Orana clans and the Griqua of South Africa, and the Gona clans within the Xhosa-speaking polities; the Richtersveld, a World Heritage Site.
f.period: proto-Khoe c. 400 BCE–100 CE in southern Zimbabwe; herding communities c. 200 BCE–300 CE, spreading south by 500 CE and south of the Orange River after 1000 CE; Portuguese contact in the 15th and 16th centuries; Dutch colonisation from the late 17th century; the Kat River Settlement 1829–1856; the genocide in German South-West Africa 1904–1907; apartheid to 1994.
f.known: herds of sheep, goats and Nguni cattle; the Battle of Salt River (1510); Khoe languages related to those of Kalahari San; the Moon in religion, and Tsui’goab and ǁGaunab; transhumance in the Richtersveld; the marksmen of the Kat River Settlement; the Nama and Damara clans and their captains
f.sources: Portuguese records of the 15th and 16th centuries; Dutch and Cape colonial records; travellers such as P. Kolben, A. Sparman, John Barrow and Emil Holub; Wilhelm Bleek’s Hottentot Fables and Tales (1864); Richard Elphick’s Khoikhoi and the Founding of White South Africa (1977); archaeology (Sadr); clan histories; genetic studies.
